steps.title: Real exchanges, everyday language
body: You already know more than enough to shop and ask for directions — this lesson doesn't teach a single new word or rule. It puts things you already know to work in two real situations.

Giving directions in Arabic often means describing where something is, not commanding someone where to go: الْبَنْكُ قَرِيبٌ، عَلَى الْيَسَارِ ("the bank is near, on the left") is exactly as natural as "turn left."

steps.title: Two everyday exchanges
steps.intro: Tap 🔊 and listen to each exchange first. Then reveal the meaning line by line.

steps.title: Shopping: the discount
steps.arabicPrompt: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ خَصْمٌ؟ — نَعَمْ، بِخَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَارًا مَعَ الْخَصْمِ
steps.explanation: The watch was بِعِشْرِينَ دِينَارًا (twenty dinars); مَعَ الْخَصْمِ (with the discount) it drops to بِخَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَارًا (fifteen).

steps.title: Shopping: paying
steps.arabicPrompt: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ نَقْدٌ أَوْ بِطَاقَةُ اِئْتِمَانٍ؟ — عِنْدِي نَقْدٌ
steps.explanation: عِنْدِي نَقْدٌ = "I have cash." نَقْد is cash; بِطَاقَةُ اِئْتِمَانٍ, the credit card, is the option the customer doesn't take.

steps.title: Directions: the bank
steps.arabicPrompt: أَيْنَ الْبَنْكُ؟ — هُوَ قَرِيبٌ. الْبَنْكُ فِي هَذَا الشَّارِعِ، عَلَى الْيَسَارِ

options.label: On this street, on the left
Straight ahead, on the second street

steps.explanation: عَلَى الْيَسَارِ = "on the left." Straight ahead on the second street (إِلَى الْأَمَامِ، فِي الشَّارِعِ الثَّانِي) is where the library is, not the bank.

steps.title: Directions: the library
steps.arabicPrompt: أَيْنَ الْمَكْتَبَةُ؟ هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيدَةٌ؟ — نَعَمْ، هِيَ بَعِيدَةٌ عَنْ هُنَا
steps.prompt: Is the library near or far?
steps.explanation: بَعِيدَةٌ عَنْ هُنَا = "far from here" — unlike the bank, which is قَرِيبٌ (near).

steps.title: You can shop and ask for directions
steps.message: Sixteen lines of real dialogue, zero new grammar — just هَلْ عِنْدَكَ...؟, مُمْكِن...؟, and location statements like عَلَى الْيَسَارِ doing real work. A2 is complete.
